gen.title: Specific heat at constant pressure versus constant volume

cells.quote: We have added a subscript “p” to the specific heat capacity to remind us that this value only applies to a constant pressure process.
where delta T (ΔT) is the change of temperature of the gas during the process, and c is the specific heat capacity.
The enthalpy, internal energy, and volume are all changed, but the pressure remains the same.

cells.value: the change of specific enthalpy is equal to the heat transfer
cells.quote: the change of specific enthalpy is equal to the heat transfer for a constant pressure process:

cells.value: c is the specific heat capacity
cells.quote: where delta T (ΔT) is the change of temperature of the gas during the process, and c is the specific heat capacity.

cells.value: the temperature change is the same
cells.quote: Even though the temperature change is the same for this process and the constant pressure process, the value of the specific heat capacity is different.
We have added a subscript “v” to the specific heat capacity to remind us that this value only applies to a constant volume process.

cells.value: the heat transfer as a constant times the change in temperature
cells.quote: And we can express the heat transfer as a constant times the change in temperature.

cells.value: the work is equal to zero
cells.quote: For a constant volume process, the work is equal to zero.
